LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 12.1.1 LISTENING TO RESPOND: ATTITUDE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 12.1: Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should one be polite when speaking over telephone?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 12.1.1 LISTENING TO RESPOND: ATTITUDE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 12.1.1 LISTENING TO RESPOND: ATTITUDE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations

What this means
In this part you learn to identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should one be polite when speaking over telephone?
2. How do we ensure politeness in a telephone conversation?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Attitude means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify polite words and phrases in telephone conversations.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
